描述_ZN: The inscription was originally carved on a cliff stone at the western foot of Jiao Mountain in Zhenjiang, Jiangsu Province, and was broken into five pieces when it was struck by lightning and fell into the Yangtze River during the Song Dynasty. It was moved to the mountain by Chen Pengnian in 1713, and later built into the wall of Ding Hui Temple. The remnants of the stone still exist today and are displayed in the pavilion of the Po Mo Xuan Monument Gallery compound. It is written in regular script, with 88 characters in total on the left line of the text, which has been lost compared to the time when it came out of the water.　　Written by Hua Yang Zhen Yi and written by Shang Huang Shan Qiao. There are many different opinions on its era and authorship. Song Su Shunqin's poem reads, "No one has seen the goose scripture in the mountains, but the crane inscription has been passed down from the mouth of the capital." It is believed to be written by Wang Xizhi of the Eastern Jin Dynasty, while some say it is written by Gu Lian of the Tang Dynasty, and others think it is written by Wang Dian of the Tang Dynasty. Huang Boshi, a famous jinshi writer in Song Dynasty, wrote it for Tao Hongjing in Liang Dynasty, while Du Mu of Ming Dynasty wrote "Golden Scallion Linlang" and Gu Yanwu of Qing Dynasty wrote "Jin Shi Writing Records".　　The inscription of "Dui He" is thick and ancient, sparse and distant. The original text on the cliff book stone, so its line of sparse, the number of words, size are not the same, jagged and interesting. The strong atmosphere of the Six Dynasties flows between the lines. Literati calligraphers of all generations have praised it a lot. Huang Tingjian of the Song Dynasty thought that "there is no larger character than the "He-Ming"". Huang Boshi cloud: "Xiao Yuan is light and elegant, if he is a person." Song Cao Shiyun Yun: "Jiao Shan's "The Inscription of a Crane" is the crown of calligraphers for its wonderful brushwork." The calligraphy of "The Inscription of the Crane" has had a great influence on later generations and has been a model for regular script since the Sui and Tang dynasties. Huang Tingjian's calligraphy is based on this.　　This topography for the National Palace Museum collection of Song topography Yang stone, before the fall of water fine topography, a total of more than 30 characters.
